mcqs.question: Which of the following statements about adipose tissue is a common misconception?

options.A: It stores fat as an energy reserve.
options.B: It provides cushioning and insulation to the body.
options.C: It is a type of connective tissue.
options.D: It lines the outer surface of the skin as a protective barrier.

mcqs.answer: It lines the outer surface of the skin as a protective barrier.
mcqs.explanation: Adipose tissue does not form the outer protective layer of the skin; that role belongs to the epidermis, an epithelial tissue. Options A, B and C correctly describe adipose tissue: it stores fat, cushions and insulates, and is classified as connective tissue. Therefore option D is the misconception.

mcqs.question: How does the loose arrangement of fibers and abundant ground substance in areolar connective tissue relate to its function in the body?

options.A: It allows rapid transmission of nerve impulses.
options.B: It provides great tensile strength to resist tearing.
options.C: It enables the tissue to act as a packing material and cushion organs.
options.D: It makes the tissue impermeable to fluids.

mcqs.answer: It enables the tissue to act as a packing material and cushion organs.
mcqs.explanation: Areolar tissue has loosely arranged collagen and elastic fibers within a gel‑like ground substance, giving it flexibility and the ability to fill spaces between organs. This structure allows it to act as a packing material and provide cushioning. Options A and D describe properties not related to areolar tissue, and option B describes dense connective tissue, not areolar.

mcqs.question: Which characteristic best distinguishes blood from other connective tissues?

options.A: Presence of a solid extracellular matrix.
options.B: Cells are suspended in a liquid extracellular matrix called plasma.
options.C: Contains dense bundles of collagen fibers.

mcqs.answer: Cells are suspended in a liquid extracellular matrix called plasma.
mcqs.explanation: Blood is unique among connective tissues because its extracellular matrix is fluid (plasma) in which cells (red cells, white cells, platelets) are suspended. Other connective tissues have solid or semi‑solid matrices. Options A, C, and D describe properties of other connective tissues such as bone or dense connective tissue.

mcqs.question: All of the following statements about bone tissue are true EXCEPT:

options.A: It contains osteocytes housed in lacunae.
options.B: Its matrix is composed mainly of calcium phosphate crystals.
options.C: It has a high capacity for regeneration due to an abundant blood supply.

mcqs.explanation: Bone matrix is a composite of inorganic calcium phosphate crystals and organic collagen fibers, which give bone both hardness and flexibility. Therefore statement D is false. Statements A, B and C correctly describe bone tissue: osteocytes reside in lacunae, the mineral component is calcium phosphate, and bone is well vascularized, allowing repair.

mcqs.question: Cartilage is best described as:

options.A: A highly vascularized tissue that stores fat.
options.B: A flexible, avascular connective tissue that provides support and reduces friction at joints.
options.C: A type of epithelial tissue forming the outer skin layer.
options.D: A liquid connective tissue that transports nutrients.

mcqs.answer: A flexible, avascular connective tissue that provides support and reduces friction at joints.
mcqs.explanation: Cartilage is an avascular (no blood vessels), flexible connective tissue composed of chondrocytes in a dense matrix of collagen and proteoglycans. It supports structures and provides smooth surfaces at joints. Options A, C, and D describe other tissue types.

mcqs.question: Which of the following correctly describes areolar connective tissue?

options.A: It is densely packed with parallel collagen fibers and provides tensile strength.
options.B: It consists of a network of fibroblasts, collagen and elastic fibers, and abundant ground substance, acting as a packing material.
options.C: It is a hard, mineralized tissue forming the skeleton.
options.D: It stores large amounts of triglycerides.

mcqs.answer: It consists of a network of fibroblasts, collagen and elastic fibers, and abundant ground substance, acting as a packing material.
mcqs.explanation: Areolar tissue has loosely arranged fibers and a gel‑like ground substance, allowing it to fill spaces and cushion organs. Option A describes dense regular tissue, option C describes bone, and option D describes adipose tissue.

mcqs.question: Adipose tissue differs from other connective tissues primarily because:

options.A: It contains a liquid matrix called plasma.
options.B: Its cells are specialized for fat storage and are called adipocytes.
options.C: It is composed mainly of densely packed collagen fibers.
options.D: It forms the protective covering of organs.

mcqs.answer: Its cells are specialized for fat storage and are called adipocytes.
mcqs.explanation: The hallmark of adipose tissue is the presence of adipocytes, which store triglycerides. The matrix is semi‑solid, not liquid (plasma belongs to blood). Dense collagen fibers characterize dense connective tissue, and organ coverings are typically serous membranes, not adipose tissue.

mcqs.question: A surgeon needs to replace a damaged ligament that connects bone to bone. Which property of dense regular connective tissue makes it most suitable for this purpose?

options.B: Parallel arrangement of collagen fibers providing great tensile strength in one direction.
options.D: Presence of many blood vessels for rapid healing.

mcqs.answer: Parallel arrangement of collagen fibers providing great tensile strength in one direction.
mcqs.explanation: Ligaments require resistance to pulling forces along a single axis; dense regular connective tissue has collagen fibers aligned parallel to the direction of stress, giving high tensile strength. Elasticity (A) is a property of elastic tissue, cushioning (C) belongs to areolar tissue, and ligaments are relatively poorly vascularized, so D is not the primary reason.
